1 Enclosure Memo for Chief of operations, Cuba Project
summary: The Joint Chiefs of Staff reviewed a memo for the Chief of Operations, Cuba Project, describing pretexts that could justify US military intervention in Cuba. They recommend forwarding it as a preliminary planning submission, with other agencies' inputs feeding a time-phased plan. They also propose that the State Department take primary responsibility for overt and covert military and paramilitary planning.

summary: OCR-garbled 1962 Joint Chiefs of Staff documents (TOP SECRET, special distribution, excluded from automatic regrading). Includes a Secretaries' note forwarding a JCS 1969/321 report on NORTHWOODS (S) for consideration by the Chiefs, and a 9 March 1962 Department of Defense JCS representative Caribbean Survey Group report to the JCS on the Cuba Project, submitted at the Chief of Operations' request, with views due 13 March 1962. Attachments are not reproduced.

title: 9 March 1962
summary: A 1962 Department of Defense report, prepared for the Joint Chiefs of Staff by the Caribbean Survey Group at the Chief of Operations' request, provides the justification for U.S. military intervention in Cuba (Top Secret). The text is largely garbled OCR, with a header marking the document as a copy with special distribution, excluded from automatic downgrading, and referencing views furnished 13 March 1962 on the Cuba Project.

title: THE PROBLEM
summary: A 1960s-era US Joint Chiefs of Staff memo on the Cuba Project asks for a brief description of a pretext that could justify US military intervention in Cuba. It notes any such pretext would lead to a political decision and then military action, references a US Navy course of action on Guantanamo incidents, and says the plan relies on heightened US-Cuban tensions to create justifiable US grievances. It also aims to portray the Cuban government as irresponsible and a threat to the Western Hemisphere to sway world and UN opinion.

summary: A 1962 US Joint Chiefs of Staff memo (Operation MONGOOSE context) on Cuba. It states that the premise for intervention holds only while US action is unlikely to draw in the USSR. Cuba has no mutual defense pact with the USSR and is not in the Warsaw Pact, so time is important. It recommends forwarding preliminary project suggestions to the Secretary of Defense, assigning one agency primary responsibility for overt and covert military plans, and restricting distribution to commanders and NATO/UN officers. The appendix lists pretexts, meant to build incidents and mask the objective, to justify US military intervention and to portray Cuba as a threat.

title: APPENDIX TO ENCLOSURE
summary: A 1962 declassified memo (Top Secret, Operation MONGOOSE, Cuba Project) requests justification pretexts for US military intervention in Cuba. It forwards project suggestions for time-phased planning, to build incidents and unrelated events that camouflage an ultimate objective and create an impression of Cuban rashness and a threat to Western Hemisphere peace. Recommends military and paramilitary responsibility be assigned to the Joint Chiefs of Staff.

title: ANNEX TO APPENDIX TO ENCLOSURE
summary: Annex to a planning appendix listing preliminary pretexts for US military intervention in Cuba. Proposes a cover-and-deception plan with harassment and feigned invasion signals, then a series of staged incidents around Guantanamo (rumors, fake Cuban attacks, sabotage, mortar fire, sunken or burned ships, mock victim funerals) meant to justify a US response: securing water and power, destroying artillery, then large-scale offensive operations.

title: 3. A "Remember the Maine" incident could be arranged
summary: Excerpt from a declassified 1962 US military planning annex (Operation Northwoods era) listing proposed pretexts to justify US intervention in Cuba: staged 'Remember the Maine' style attacks on US ships or drones blamed on Cuba; a fake Communist Cuban terror campaign against Florida and Washington refugees; a simulated Cuban-backed filibuster against Caribbean neighbors; false MIG provocations and staged hijackings; a faked shootdown of a chartered civilian airliner; a staged downing of a USAF F-101 over international waters; and the JCS's stated need for a Cuban 'provocation' if internal revolt fails.

title: ENCLOSURE B
summary: A declassified enclosure on Cuba (1962) states that the Joint Chiefs of Staff previously held that unilateral US military intervention in Cuba could follow hostile Cuban acts against US forces or property as a pretext. It quotes JCS's 7 March 1962 view that if covert efforts to foster an internal Cuban revolt fail, the US must create a Cuban 'provocation' to justify military action. It notes the State Department is also preparing courses of action to justify intervention.
